projects.title: Job Portal
projects.subtitle: Making the job hunt feel effortless
projects.overview: An end-to-end job platform designed so discovery feels effortless and applying takes seconds. The work spans research, flows, wireframes, a design system and a high-fidelity prototype.
projects.problem: Seekers abandon portals when search feels heavy and applications take too many steps. The interface needed to make discovery effortless and applying obvious — without burying people in filters.
projects.research: I interviewed eight active job seekers and mapped their journey end to end. Three friction points dominated: noisy, unclear filters; job cards that hid the details people actually decide on; and multi-page application forms that killed momentum right before submission.

projects.title: Merch Commerce
projects.subtitle: A streetwear drop that checks out in two taps
projects.overview: A limited-drop commerce experience built around urgency without chaos — browse, pick a size and check out before the hype fades.
projects.problem: Limited drops create pressure. If size selection or checkout stalls for even a moment, carts are abandoned. The flow had to feel instant and confident.
projects.research: I studied drop culture and cart-abandonment patterns across five stores. The recurring winner was a countdown-led hero paired with a two-tap size-and-checkout path that never leaves the product context.

personas.name: Rhea
personas.bio: Follows drops, buys in the first minutes, shops on mobile only.

feedback.quote: It feels like the product never lets go of you until you've bought it.
feedback.name: Usability tester

projects.title: Content Studio
projects.subtitle: A calm command center for a chaotic content calendar
projects.overview: A content-operations dashboard that turns a high-volume social calendar into a calm, glanceable system — status at a glance, fast handoffs, zero guesswork.
projects.problem: A high-volume brand shipped content weekly but had no single view of what was live, drafted or overdue. Status lived in people's heads and DMs.
projects.research: I shadowed the content team through two full weeks. The core need was status-at-a-glance and frictionless handoffs — the tool had to fit their existing rituals, not replace them.

personas.name: Devi
personas.bio: Owns the calendar, unblocks the team, reports to the brand.

personas.name: Sam

feedback.quote: For the first time the whole team can see the week without asking anyone.
